rows.speaker: المفردات
rows.claim: The lexicon derives omen-taking from divination by birds, then extends it to anything treated as a good or bad omen.
rows.anchor: تطير فلان واطير أصله التفاؤل بالطير ثم يستعمل في كل ما يتفاءل به ويتشاءم

rows.speaker: المفردات
rows.claim: The verb for people dispersing can also mean that they hurry.
rows.anchor: ويقال تطايروا إذا أسرعوا ويقال إذا تفرقوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In context, a person's bird is what indicates the good or bad outcome awaiting him.
rows.anchor: سياق ما قبل الآية وما بعدها وخاصة قوله { من اهتدى فإنما يهتدي لنفسه } الخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The neck signifies attachment because a person cannot separate from it, unlike the limbs, and anything hung there immediately faces him.
rows.anchor: وإنما جعل الإلزام في العنق لأنه العضو الذي لا يمكن أن يفارقه الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The attached bird is each person's acquired deed, which remains with him and determines his felicity or misery by God's decree.
rows.anchor: فالمراد بقوله { وكل إنسان ألزمناه طائره في عنقه } أن الذي يستعقب لكل إنسان سعادته أو شقاءه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person's deed belongs to that person, who receives its full recompense, as the cited passage on human striving says.
rows.anchor: وهذا هو العمل الذي يعمله الإنسان لقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ordained pattern makes good outcomes follow faith and piety, and bad outcomes follow disbelief and disobedience.
rows.anchor: أن حسن العاقبة للإيمان والتقوى وسوء العاقبة للكفر والمعصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse ties felicity and misery to freely acquired good and bad deeds; it does not endorse an eternal decree independent of whether one acts or obeys.
rows.anchor: من جهة أعماله الحسنة والسيئة المكتسبة من طريق الاختيار من دون أن يبطل تأثير العمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The displayed book is each person's own record and contains every deed without omission.
rows.anchor: أن الكتاب الذي يخرج له هو كتابه نفسه لا يتعلق بغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The record shows deeds in their true realities, with their good or evil results exposed beyond concealment or excuse.
rows.anchor: وثالثا أن الأعمال التي أحصاها بادية فيها بحقائقها من سعادة أو شقاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The record contains the actual deeds themselves, made visible to the person, rather than written symbols like ordinary books.
rows.anchor: أن الكتاب يتضمن نفس الأعمال بحقائقها دون الرسوم المخطوطة على حد الكتب المعمولة فيما بيننا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bird and book refer to the same deed; calling it a book at resurrection avoids suggesting it only then becomes a book or was previously hidden despite clinging to its owner.
rows.anchor: أن المراد بالطائر والكتاب في الآية أمر واحد وهو العمل الذي يعمله الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God brings the book out from behind heedlessness on Judgment Day and makes its details visible, already prepared for its owner.
rows.anchor: كتاب الأعمال بحقائقها مستور عن إدراك الإنسان محجوب وراء حجاب الغفلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The book confirms that a person will inevitably meet the consequences of his deeds, since they both cling to him and will be openly displayed.
rows.anchor: الإنسان ستناله تبعة عمله لا محالة أما أولا فلأنه لازم له لا يفارقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the phrase كفى بنفسك, the bāʾ is emphatic and زائد; the feminine verb may take masculine agreement because its subject is grammatically feminine but not natural feminine.
rows.anchor: الباء فيه زائدة للتأكيد وأصله كفت نفسك وإنما لم يؤنث الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative grammatical analysis treats كفى as an indeclinable verb meaning اكتف and the bāʾ as non زائد.
rows.anchor: وربما قيل إنه اسم فعل بمعنى اكتف والباء غير زائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The record is conclusive evidence even against the sinner who reads it, because he directly witnesses the deed and its recompense.
rows.anchor: حجة للكتاب قاطعة بحيث لا يرتاب فيها قارئه ولو كان هو المجرم نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surrounding rebuke links human haste to the record of deeds: people fail to distinguish benefit from harm and rush after desires, though every deed remains with its doer and will be reviewed.
rows.anchor: أنزل القرآن وجعله هاديا إلى ملة هي أقوم جريا على السنة الإلهية في هداية الناس

rows.speaker: المفردات
rows.claim: The word وزر means a burden, metaphorically used for sin as a burden to carry.
rows.anchor: الوزر الثقل تشبيها بوزر الجبل، ويعبر بذلك عن الإثم كما يعبر عنه بالثقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance benefits its follower and misguidance harms that same person; one soul cannot transfer its own burden to another.
rows.anchor: فمن اهتدى فإنما يهتدي لنفسه وينتفع به نفسه من غير أن يتبع غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Misguiding leaders and initiators of evil practices bear additional burdens for their leadership or precedent, not the identical burden transferred from followers.
rows.anchor: لكن ذلك كله وزر الإمامة وجعل السنة وتحمل الخطايا لا عين ما للعامل من الوزر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The context and past-tense formulation indicate worldly annihilation punishment: God's historical practice was to destroy a people only after sending a warner.
rows.anchor: الظاهر في أنه كانت السنة الإلهية في الأمم الخالية الهالكة جارية على أن لا يعذبهم إلا بعد أن يبعث إليهم رسولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A messenger, unlike a prophet in the author's earlier distinction, holds a special office that ends an ummah's case in destruction or reprieve.
rows.anchor: أن الرسالة منصب خاص إلهي يستعقب الحكم الفصل في الأمة إما بعذاب الاستئصال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the envoy a messenger specifies worldly annihilation punishment, rather than afterlife punishment or punishment without qualification.
rows.anchor: فالتعبير بالرسول لإفادة أن المراد نفي التعذيب الدنيوي دون التعذيب الأخروي أو مطلق التعذيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse answers the impression that every sin automatically brings worldly or otherworldly punishment: divine mercy withholds extermination until a messenger warns and completes the proof.
rows.anchor: لا يعذب الناس بعذاب الاستئصال وهو عذاب الدنيا إلا بعد أن يبعث رسولا ينذرهم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse reports a merciful divine practice, not a rational rule that makes pre-message punishment impossible; it denies that such punishment occurs, not that it is permissible.
rows.anchor: فالآية - كما ترى - ليست مسوقة لإمضاء حكم العقل بقبح العقاب بلا بيان بل هي تكشف عن اقتضاء العناية الإلهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rationally evident religious roots such as God's oneness, prophethood, and resurrection ground accountability without prophetic exposition, while practical branches require prophetic clarification for afterlife reward and punishment.
rows.anchor: أصول الدين وهي التي يستقل العقل ببيانها ويتفرع عليها قبول الفروع التي تتضمنها الدعوة النبوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worldly extermination punishment discussed above requires a messenger by divine care, not because reason forbids it before the message.
rows.anchor: والمؤاخذة الدنيوية بعذاب الاستئصال يتوقف على بعث الرسول بعناية من الله سبحانه لا لحكم عقلي

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: The affluent are people expanded in material blessing, as characterized by the cited description of a person whose Lord tests, honors, and enriches him.
rows.anchor: الترفة التوسع في النعمة يقال أترف فلان فهو مترف

rows.speaker: ابن عرفة
rows.claim: A مُترف is someone left free to do whatever he wants without restraint.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عرفة المترف المتروك يصنع ما يشاء ولا يمنع منه

rows.speaker: المجمع
rows.claim: The lexicon glosses تدمير as destruction and دمار as ruin.
rows.anchor: وقال التدمير الإهلاك والدمار الهلاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression about God willing a town's destruction means that its time of destruction has drawn near, as in idioms about illness and rain approaching.
rows.anchor: أي إذا دنا وقت هلاكهم من قبيل قولهم إذا أراد العليل أن يموت كان كذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author also allows active divine will to mean that the causes of destruction have converged, especially ingratitude and tyrannical wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: ويمكن أن يراد به الإرادة الفعلية وحقيقتها توافق الأسباب المقتضية للشيء وتعاضدها على وقوعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not legislatively command indecency, and a creative command to sin would eliminate choice and thus the possibility of sin.
rows.anchor: لا يأمر بالمعصية أمرا تشريعيا فهو القائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A creative command cannot target sin because it would make the act necessary and remove the human choice required for disobedience.
rows.anchor: إنما أمره إذا أراد شيئا أن يقول له كن فيكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the command concerns obedience, it is the genuine legislative order delivered by a messenger; the people disobey, incur the threatened judgment, and are destroyed.
rows.anchor: كان الأمر بحقيقة معناه وهو الأمر التشريعي وكان هو الأمر الذي توجه إليهم بلسان الرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the command concerns sin, it is figurative: God lavishly supplies blessings through respite and enticement, drawing the affluent toward transgression until judgment falls.
rows.anchor: كان الأمر مرادا به الإكثار من إفاضة النعم عليهم وتوفيرها على سبيل الإملاء والاستدراج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first reading is less plausible because the wording appears to make the command concern the very act that follows, and because only the affluent are addressed although the whole town must sin for it to be destroyed.
rows.anchor: ظاهره تعلق الأمر بعين ما فرع عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first reading also has no clear reason to single out the affluent when the whole town's wrongdoing brings destruction.
rows.anchor: عدم ظهور وجه لتعلق الأمر بالمترفين مع كون الفسق لجميع أهل القرية

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari reads the command metaphorically as abundant blessings that the affluent turn into means of sin, although God gave them to prompt gratitude and good works.
rows.anchor: صب عليهم النعمة صبا فجعلوها ذريعة إلى المعاصي واتباع الشهوات

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari argues that ففسقوا identifies the deleted command's object as sin, since ordinary usage makes the following act the understood command.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن المأمور به إنما حذف لأن فسقوا يدل عليه وهو كلام مستفيض يقال أمرته فقام وأمرته فقرأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says al-Zamakhshari establishes the wording's apparent direction, not that the verse can only mean a command to sin.
rows.anchor: وأما كونه صريحا فيه بحيث لا يحتمل إلا ذلك كما يدعيه فلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternative can be like saying someone was ordered but disobeyed, so فسقوا signals an order to obey; alternatively the order was directed to them and they sinned against it.
rows.anchor: أمرته فعصاني حيث تكون المعصية وهي منافية للأمر قرينة على كون المأمور به هو الطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both readings of the command are possible, though the reading that the command concerns sin has greater surface plausibility.
rows.anchor: فالحق أن الوجهين لا بأس بكل منهما وإن كان الثاني لا يخلو من ظهور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some explain why the affluent alone are addressed by treating them as leaders whose followers share their ruling; the author finds this explanation weak.
rows.anchor: بأنهم الرؤساء السادة والأئمة المتبوعون وغيرهم أتباعهم وحكم التابع تابع لحكم المتبوع ولا يخلو من سقم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some treat the command clause as a description of the town and supply an omitted conditional answer; others reverse the order, but the author calls that reversal implausible.
rows.anchor: وذكر آخرون أن في الآية تقديما وتأخيرا والتقدير وإذا أمرنا مترفي قرية ففسقوا فيها أردنا أن نهلكها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The standard light reading of أمرنا derives from command; another proposed derivation takes it to mean that God increased the affluent in wealth and children.
rows.anchor: هذا كله على القراءة المعروفة { أمرنا } بفتح الهمزة ثم الميم مخففة من الأمر بمعنى الطلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A long-vowel reading آمرنا is attributed to Ali, Asim, Ibn Kathir, Nafi, and others, meaning abundance of wealth or an order to act.
rows.anchor: وقرئ { آمرنا } بالمد ونسب إلى علي عليه السلام والى عاصم وابن كثير ونافع وغيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A geminated-mim reading أمرنا means appointing as commanders and is attributed to Ali, al-Hasan, al-Baqir, Ibn Abbas, Zayd ibn Ali, and others.
rows.anchor: وقرئ أيضا { أمرنا } بتشديد الميم من التأمير بمعنى تولية الإمارة ونسب ذلك إلى علي والحسن والباقر عليهم السلام

rows.speaker: المفردات
rows.claim: The lexicon defines a قرن as people living together in one time-period and gives قرون as its plural.
rows.anchor: القرن القوم المقترنون في زمن واحد وجمعه قرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The destruction of earlier generations confirms the divine practice just described; the verse suggests this practice began among human generations after Noah.
rows.anchor: وفيها تثبيت ما ذكر في الآية السابقة من سنة الله الجارية في إهلاك القرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before Noah, humanity lived in the simplicity of original nature; people began to differ afterward.
rows.anchor: أن المجتمع الإنساني قبل زمن نوح عليه السلام كانوا على سذاجة الفطرة ثم اختلفوا بعد ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿājila is an omitted noun's adjective, probably worldly life because it contrasts with the afterlife next; others say it means immediate blessings or transient worldly goods.
rows.anchor: العاجلة صفة محذوفة الموصوف ولعل موصوفها الحياة بقرينة مقابلتها للآخرة

rows.speaker: المفردات
rows.claim: The lexicon explains ṣaly as kindling or enduring the heat of fire, while ṣallā can mean entering it and aṣlā can mean causing someone to enter it.
rows.anchor: وفي المفردات أصل الصلي لإيقاد النار. قال وقال الخليل صلى الكافر النار قاسى حرها

rows.speaker: المجمع
rows.claim: The lexicon defines being driven away as expulsion and distance.
rows.anchor: الدحر الإبعاد والمدحور المبعد المطرود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After discussing worldly destruction following a prophetic mission, the passage turns to afterlife punishment, reward, and the general principle governing both.
rows.anchor: عاد إلى بيان سنته في التعذيب الأخروي والإثابة فيها في هذه الآية والآيتين بعدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wanting worldly life means seeking its pleasures as an independent end; using the world as a route to afterlife happiness is itself pursuit of the afterlife.
rows.anchor: إنما يعد طلبا لها إذا كانت مقصودة بالاستقلال لا لأجل التوسل بها إلى سعادة الأخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The continuing expression من كان يريد describes someone persistently devoted to this material life, neglecting the afterlife and thereby emptying belief and religion of purpose.
rows.anchor: حيث يدل على استمرار الإرادة. وهذا هو الذي لا يرى لنفسه إلا هذه الحياة المادية الدنيوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God hastens to the worldly seeker only what He chooses, for whom He chooses; human desire does not govern divine allocation.
rows.anchor: لكن لا بإعطائه ما يريده بل بإعطائه ما نريده فالأمر إلينا لا إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly seekers receive what the surrounding causes permit; their requests by the language of their condition yield only what those causes lead to.
rows.anchor: يرزق منها على حسب ما تسمح له الأسباب والعوامل التي أجراها الله في الكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A passage about silver roofs for disbelievers shows that worldly wealth follows the shared causal order and has no value in the afterlife's scale.
rows.anchor: ولا فرق بين الكافر والمؤمن قبال العلل الكونية بل من صادفته أسباب الغنى والثروة أثرته وأغنته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading that one wants the world specifically through one's deeds is an unsupported restriction drawn from Hud; that passage concerns recompense for deeds, while this passage contrasts life-goals.
rows.anchor: وهو تقييد من غير مقيد، ولعله أخذه من قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worldly seeker is made to enter Hell, disgraced and expelled from mercy; these descriptions indicate exclusion from forgiveness and mercy.
rows.anchor: والقيدان يفيدان أنه مخصوص بجهنم محروم من المغفرة والرحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attachment to this world and denial of the next have degrees: some show them in both word and deed, others in deed while verbally acknowledging the afterlife.
rows.anchor: فمن ذلك ما هو كذلك قولا وفعلا ومنه ما هو كذلك فعلا مع الاعتراف به قولا

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Saʿy means brisk walking, less than running, and is also used for earnest effort toward good or evil.
rows.anchor: السعي المشي السريع وهو دون العدو، ويستعمل للجد في الأمر خيرا كان أو شرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife sought here means the next life itself, and the earlier argument also rejects narrowing the phrase to intending it through one's deeds.
rows.anchor: أي الحياة الآخرة نظير ما تقدم من قوله { من كان يريد العاجلة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The possessive wording makes the effort specific to the afterlife: one must strive in a manner fitting for it, exerting full effort in good deeds grounded in certain reason or legal proof.
rows.anchor: ويستفاد منه أن سعيه لها يجب أن يكون سعيا يليق بها ويحق لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Belief means God and entails divine oneness, prophethood, and resurrection; the explicit condition requires sound belief including tawhid and acknowledgment of prophethood.
rows.anchor: فإن من لا يعترف بإحدى الخصال الثلاث لا يعده الله سبحانه في كلامه مؤمنا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God thanks the believers' effort by accepting it well and praising its doer; both reward and subsequent praise are grace, with praise being grace upon grace.
rows.anchor: وقوله { فأولئك كان سعيهم مشكورا } أي يشكره الله بحسن قبوله والثناء على ساعيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Afterlife-directed deeds reliably reach their ends, unlike worldly causes, since God says the effort is thanked but worldly provision is only what He wills for whom He wills.
rows.anchor: وفي الآيتين دلالة على أن الأسباب الأخروية وهي الأعمال لا تتخلف عن غاياتها بخلاف الأسباب الدنيوية

rows.speaker: المفردات
rows.claim: The root of مدّ is extension; adding a supply to something from its own kind prolongs its duration, as a spring is replenished from its source.
rows.anchor: فإمداد الشيء ومده أن يضاف إليه من نوعه مثلا ما يمتد به بقاؤه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God supplies the prerequisites of every action—knowledge, will, bodily powers, tools, materials, causes, and conditions—without which human action could not occur.
rows.anchor: كل ذلك أمور تكوينية لا صنع للإنسان فيها ولو فقد كلها أو بعضها لم يكن العمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both worldly and afterlife seekers draw on God's gifts; if that provision stopped, their actions would stop, and their misuse of it leaves blame on themselves.
rows.anchor: فأهل الدنيا في دنياهم وأهل الآخرة في آخرتهم يستمدون من عطائه تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object كلاً is fronted for emphasis, and هؤلاء وهؤلاء denotes the two groups: those given worldly gains and those whose effort is thanked.
rows.anchor: وإنما قدم المفعول على فعله لتعلق العناية به في الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both groups remain under divine care; one uses the gift to seek the afterlife and is thanked, while the other seeks the immediate world, forgets the afterlife, and ends in misery.
rows.anchor: غير أن أحدهما يستعمل النعمة الإلهية لابتغاء الآخرة فيشكر الله سعيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All the means on which people rely in their work come from God's gift, since neither people nor other creatures create them.
rows.anchor: فإن جميع ما يستفيدون منه في أعمالهم كما تقدم لا صنع لهم ولا لغيرهم من المخلوقين فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because both groups act through God's gifts, using them for unbelief and sin merits reproach, while using them in faith and obedience merits divine thanks.
rows.anchor: فحقيق على من يستعمل نعمته في الكفر والفسوق أن يصلى النار مذموما مدحورا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The twice-repeated shift to ربك highlights that provision is an aspect of God's unique lordship, against idolaters' claims of other lords.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله { ربك } التفات من التكلم مع الغير إلى الغيبة وقد كرر ذلك مرتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's giving is unrestricted; variations and apparent limits arise from each recipient's capacity or lack of readiness, not from the giver.
rows.anchor: فإنما هو من ناحية المستفيض وخصوص استعداده للاستفاضة أو فقدانه من رأس لا من ناحية المفيض

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan is reported to limit the shared gift to worldly provision, with afterlife reward reserved for believers.
rows.anchor: ما نسب إلى الحسن وقتادة أن المراد بالعطاء العطاء الدنيوي

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada is likewise reported to understand the shared gift as worldly provision only.
rows.anchor: ما نسب إلى الحسن وقتادة أن المراد بالعطاء العطاء الدنيوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects that restriction: the wording is unrestricted and concerns provision sustaining actions, not rewards; limits stem from recipients, and even afterlife gifts are not barred by God.
rows.anchor: وفيه أنه تقييد من غير مقيد مع صلاحية المورد للإطلاق

rows.speaker: روح المعاني
rows.claim: A reported taxonomy divides agents into those seeking this world, the afterlife, both, or neither; mixed motives then divide according to which desire predominates or whether they are equal.
rows.anchor: والتقسيم الحاصر أن كل فاعل إما أن يريد بفعله العاجلة فقط أو يريد الآخرة فقط أو يريدهما معا

rows.speaker: روح المعاني
rows.claim: The reported discussion says scholars disagree over accepting mixed-motive deeds when afterlife intent predominates, but agree against deeds where worldly motive predominates or ties.
rows.anchor: ونقل اختلاف العلماء في قبول هذا النوع من العمل، ونقل اتفاقهم على عدم قبول ما يترجح فيه باعث الدنيا

rows.speaker: روح المعاني
rows.claim: The fourth type is impossible for those who require every voluntary act to have a motive; others say such an act has no inner effect but remains outwardly forbidden.
rows.anchor: وأما القسم الرابع عند القائلين بأن صدور الفعل من القادر يتوقف على حصول الداعي فهو ممتنع الحصول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These verses classify a person's ultimate life-goal, not the acceptance of every individual act: seeking this world treats it as the end, while seeking the afterlife treats this world as a stage toward it.
rows.anchor: أن الآيات الكريمة ليست في مقام بيان حكم الرد والقبول بالنسبة إلى كل عمل صدر عن عامل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Afterlife-seekers can still fail to strive properly or lack belief, but the verse selects the believing person whose effort fits the afterlife because it identifies the roots of happiness and misery.
rows.anchor: ولم يذكر في كلامه تعالى إلا حكم طائفة خاصة وهي من أراد الآخرة وسعى لها سعيها وهو مؤمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Differences in rank correspond to differences in effort; treating slight and abundant, or poor and excellent, work alike would erase the basis of preference.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى تفاوت الدرجات بتفاوت المساعي حتى لا يتوهم أن قليل العمل وكثيره على حد سواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first comparison concerns worldly differences in wealth, status, children, strength, reputation, authority, and public acceptance.
rows.anchor: والتفضيل في الدنيا هو ما يزيد به بعض أهلها على بعض من أعراضها وأمتعتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Afterlife ranks exceed worldly ones: worldly differences arise from limited competing causes, while afterlife rank reflects inner faith and sincerity, whose variations far exceed bodily differences.
rows.anchor: سبب التفضيل في الدنيا هي اختلاف الأسباب الكونية وهي محدودة والدار دار التزاحم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly differences shape people's inner perceptions, intentions, and deeds, which in turn produce their different afterlife ranks; looking at earthly distinctions helps infer the greater distinctions to come.
rows.anchor: فإن اختلاف الأحوال في الدنيا يؤدي إلى اختلاف الإدراكات الباطنة والنيات والأعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition of associating another god with God concludes the preceding contrast: shirk leaves a person stuck, disgraced, and without divine help on the path toward closeness.
rows.anchor: والمعنى لا تشرك بالله سبحانه حتى يؤديك ذلك إلى أن تقعد وتحتبس عن السير إلى درجات القرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes sitting as a figure for humiliation and incapacity.
rows.anchor: وقيل القعود كناية عن المذلة والعجز

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: In a report through Abu Amr al-Zubayri, Abu Abd Allah explains that the Quran guides to the most upright path by calling people to it.
rows.anchor: بإسناده عن أبي عمرو الزبيري عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Al-Fudayl ibn Yasar reports from Abu Jaʿfar that the Quran guides to wilayah; the author treats this as an application that may mean the Imam's complete religious knowledge or the Imam himself.
rows.anchor: عن الفضيل بن يسار عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: In a report through Abu al-Jarud, Abu Jaʿfar says a person's good and evil remain with him wherever he goes until he receives the record of his deeds.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية أبي الجارود عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: A report from Zurarah, Humran, and Muhammad ibn Muslim, citing Abu Jaʿfar and Abu Abd Allah, explains the attached bird as a person's allotted measure or destiny.
rows.anchor: عن زرارة وحمران ومحمد بن مسلم عن أبي جعفر وأبي عبد الله عليهما السلام عن الآية

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Khalid ibn Yahya reports that the servant recalls every deed and its record as if doing it at that moment, explaining the complaint that nothing small or large is omitted.
rows.anchor: عن خالد بن يحيى عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Humran reports Abu Jaʿfar reading أمرنا with a doubled mim as meaning that God increased the affluent; a second report has him gloss it as commanding their leading figures.
rows.anchor: عن حمران عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام في قوله { أمرنا مترفيها } مشددة منصوبة تفسيرها كثرنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author omits reports on these verses transmitted through both Sunni and Shiʿi routes from the Prophet, Ali, Salman, and others because they lack Quranic, prophetic, or decisive rational support and have weak chains.
rows.anchor: روايات تركنا إيرادها لعدم تأيدها بكتاب أو سنة أو حجة عقلية قاطعة مع ما فيها من ضعف الأسناد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qada first means resolving a matter whose outcome is undetermined: when all causes and conditions are complete, one side becomes fixed and ambiguity ends.
rows.anchor: خرجت من التردد والإبهام وتعين لها أحد الطرفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same distinction applies to human choices, legal ownership disputes, and speech: a ruling or report fixes one side after uncertainty, which is the basic sense of qada.
rows.anchor: وهذا المعنى هو الذي نسميه القضاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because created events depend on God, their determination when causes and conditions are complete is God's qada; the same term applies to decisive legislation.
rows.anchor: كان ذلك تعيينا منه تعالى وفصلا لها من الجانب الآخر وقطعا للإبهام، ويسمى قضاء من الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quranic qada refers both to creative determination and to legislative judgment, and can also be expressed as God's decisive judgment or word.
rows.anchor: فالآيات الكريمة - كما ترى - تمضى صحة هذين الاعتبارين العقليين في الأشياء الكونية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By causality, a contingent thing is necessary relative to its complete cause but remains possible when considered in itself or relative to an incomplete cause; this necessary determination is qada.
rows.anchor: إذا نسب إلى علته التامة كان له منها الضرورة والوجوب إذ ما لم يجب لم يوجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: General necessity across contingent beings is God's general qada and each being's particular necessity is its specific qada; qada is an active attribute inferred from the effect's relation to its complete cause.
rows.anchor: ومن هنا يظهر أن القضاء من صفاته الفعلية وهو منتزع من الفعل

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: A report from Hisham ibn Salim says that when God wants something, He measures it, decrees it, and then brings it to pass.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبد الله عليه السلام أن الله إذا أراد شيئا قدره فإذا قدره قضاه فإذا قضاه أمضاه

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن
rows.claim: In a report to Yunus, Abu al-Hasan corrects the ordering of will, desire, measure, decree, and enactment, and explains measurement as dimensions and duration.
rows.anchor: إن الله إذا شاء شيئا أراده وإذا أراد قدره وإذا قدره قضاه وإذا قضاه أمضاه الحديث

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن
rows.claim: Another Yunus report distinguishes willing as initiating an act, intending as persisting in it, measuring as setting its dimensions, and decreeing as making it irreversible.
rows.anchor: قلت فما معنى شاء؟ قال ابتداء الفعل. قلت فما معنى أراد؟ قال الثبوت عليه.

rows.speaker: العالم
rows.claim: A report through al-Muʿalla orders knowledge, will, intent, measure, decree, and enactment; once decree is enacted there is no further badaʾ.
rows.anchor: فالعلم متقدم على المشيئة والمشيئة ثانية والإرادة ثالثة والتقدير واقع على القضاء بالامضاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence among knowledge, will, intent, and the later stages is a rational ordering based on how each concept is inferred.
rows.anchor: والذي ذكره عليه السلام من ترتب المشيئة على العلم والإرادة على المشيئة وهكذا ترتب عقلي بحسب صحة الانتزاع

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali explains that he moved away from a leaning wall by fleeing from divine qada to qadar: qadar does not make an outcome unavoidable, whereas qada cannot be averted.
rows.anchor: أفر من قضاء الله إلى قدر الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The divine outpouring is unlimited because the necessary existent is absolute; a bounded effect would imply limitation and composition in its unbounded source.
rows.anchor: أطبقت البراهين على أن وجود الواجب تعالى بما أنه واجب لذاته مطلق غير محدود بحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since the created effect must accord with its cause, divine existence as a single source yields an unbounded unified effect; apparent lack and fullness belong to recipients.
rows.anchor: فما يتراءى في الممكنات من جهات الاختلاف التي تقضي بالتحديد من النقص والكمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Species-level differences arise from the different receptive essences of beings, while individual differences in later perfections arise from material readiness and preparatory causes.
rows.anchor: فمنشأها ما هيأتها القابلة للوجود بإمكانها الذاتي كالإنسان والفرس المختلفين في نوعيهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source's emanation is one and unlimited, while different recipients transform it according to their capacities, like bodies receiving the same sunlight differently.
rows.anchor: كالشمس التي تفيض نورا واحدا متشابه الأجزاء لكن الأجسام القابلة لنورها تتصرف فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection says real differences must either rest on unreal essences and capacities, which cannot explain them, or on real existence, which would make them effects of God and undermine the thesis.
rows.anchor: فإن قلت لا ريب في أن هذه الاختلافات أمور واقعية فإن كان ما عد منشأ لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reply is that this objection dissolves differences into one existence: distinctions such as possession and lack result from analyzing existence into essence, potency, and actuality, so the unbounded source remains one.
rows.anchor: أما إذا رجع الجميع إلى الوجود الذي هو حقيقة واحدة مطلقة لم يبق للبحث عن سبب الاختلاف محل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The listed universal religious precepts follow the Quran's declaration that it guides to the most upright way.
rows.anchor: بيان عدة من كليات الدين يذكرها الله سبحانه وهي تتبع قوله قبل آيات { إن هذا القرآن يهدي للتي هي أقوم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction can be parsed as negation plus exception with أن as a verbal noun, or as a prohibition with an exceptive phrase and أن as verbal noun or explicative; either resolves into worshipping God alone with sincerity.
rows.anchor: وعلى أي حال ينحل مجموع المستثنى والمستثنى منه إلى جملتين كقولنا تعبدونه ولا تعبدون غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here qada is decisive legislative judgment: it applies to commands and prohibitions and establishes affirmative or negative rulings conclusively.
rows.anchor: وهو القضاء التشريعي المتعلق بالأحكام والقضايا التشريعية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worshipping God alone is the greatest religious command and shirk the gravest major sin; all disobedience derives from obeying devils, desires, or ignorance, since obedience itself is worship.
rows.anchor: والإخلاص بالعبادة أوجب الواجبات كما أن معصيته وهو الشرك بالله سبحانه أكبر الكبائر الموبقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even an atheist is a kind of associator because he entrusts the world's governance to matter, nature, time, or another substitute while innate nature acknowledges the Creator.
rows.anchor: حتى أن الكافر المنكر للصانع مشرك بإلقائه زمام تدبير العالم إلى المادة أو الطبيعة أو الدهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to honor parents is attached to the preceding command: God decrees or commands that people treat their parents with goodness.
rows.anchor: عطف على سابقه أي وقضى ربك بأن تحسنوا بالوالدين إحسانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After exclusive worship, kindness to parents is the most obligatory duty and disobedience to them the gravest sin after shirk, explaining its placement before the remaining precepts.
rows.anchor: وهذا بعد التوحيد لله من أوجب الواجبات كما أن عقوقهما أكبر الكبائر بعد الشرك بالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parental bond and affection between parents and children sustain human society and naturally keep spouses together; honoring parents preserves this social foundation, while abandoning it dissolves the family bond and society.
rows.anchor: الرابطة العاطفية المتوسطة بين الأب والأم من جانب والولد من جانب آخر من أعظم ما يقوم به المجتمع الإنساني على ساقه
